rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Fresh walk of every pronoun/demonstrative per chunk against current body (body_sha unchanged from prior judged version, re-derived rather than carried). Chunks 2-7: every 'it'/'its'/'that whole shape'/'the first' resolves inside its own chunk to a noun named in the same or immediately preceding clause (the agent, a whole task shape, the second task's predecessor, one task, the loop, a working loop/its surroundings). Line 39 'held by calibration, the checking of the checks' is the term's first appearance, but the appositive 'the checking of the checks' glosses it in the same clause, so it does not depend on Part 2 to resolve -- a deliberate quiet-clue per the maintainer note, not an unresolved forward reference. Chunk 8 line 55 'Unmeasured green' is a fresh noun phrase (CI-green idiom), not a pronoun pointing at prior text, so it is outside rule 1's scope (dialect is rule 8's lane, and 'green' there is ordinary engineering shorthand). Chunk 9 line 62 'Read the doors again' and 'an unfamiliar codebase' are same-file callbacks to the 'The door is trust...' seams (chunks 2-6) and chunk 3's codebase line -- both explicitly allowed by the NOT-violations clause (term introduced earlier in the same file, reused). No never-named, vague-with-full-history, or re-chunk-stranded referent found.

The file's only two links are named by title inline, not positioned: line 9 '[The AI-Native Engineering Playbook: Crawl, Walk, Run, Fly]' and line 56 '[This is getting ridiculous: I shipped 490 pull requests in June]'. No 'the opening lecture said' / 'earlier in this course' style positional phrasing anywhere in body; no navigational pointer to another in-repo document at all (§2's carve-out is therefore not in play either way).

Every chunk carries a self-carrying claim: chunk 0 states the discipline in one sentence; each level chunk (2-7) states the level's work plus a three-beat Moves-you-up seam; chunk 8 carries the diagram plus four defining bullets and the Wollsen data point; chunk 9 states the model's unity. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Checked each header against its own chunk body: 'Assistance' -> 'AI helps with work already on your desk' (13); 'Interactive work' -> 'One conversation, one task' (19); 'Delegating bounded outcomes' -> 'You hand over an outcome, not a step' (25); 'Directing parallel sessions' -> 'You direct several sessions rather than one conversation' (31); 'Encoding checked loops' -> 'Recurring work becomes a loop with its own checks' (37); 'Improving the system' -> 'You improve the context, memory, skills, and verification' (43); 'Part 2: The leverage model' -> diagram + Reach/Calibration bullets (49-54); 'One model, not two' -> 'The progression and the leverage model describe the same thing' (62). No header contradicted by its own content.

Checked all six sub-items against the current wording, per chunk. No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere. Closest candidate for the anaphora/epistrophe ban is line 33 'the same handoffs, the same checks, the same merge discipline' -- a single-sentence three-item list, not the rule's cited cross-sentence tic ('Every session... Every session... Every session...'), and its third leg ('merge discipline') is new concrete content distinct from the first two, so it clears the rule's own third-leg-new-content test either way. No self-grading superlatives -- 'far below the multiple suggested by its pull-request count' (56) is a stated finding about a ratio, not self-praise; value-prop-leak sub-item PASS. Numeric claims (six levels; 30-40 sessions; 10-15 managed; three-to-four-times value) each stand with their label, no self-retraction pattern ('could be more, could be less'). No abstraction-noun stacks: 'calibrated agency' / 'reckless autonomy' are the diagram's own precisely-defined quadrant labels, not vague padding. No verb triplets with an empty leg anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule is scoped to '- ' bullets; the only bulleted content in the file is chunk 8, lines 51-54 (all prose elsewhere, incl. the '**Moves you up:**' seams, is paragraph text, not a bullet, so out of this rule's literal scope). Checked each of the four bullets against all three classes. (a) doctrine restatement: bullets 1-2 ('**Reach** is how much you delegate...', '**Calibration** is whether trust...', 51-52) are the FIRST formal naming of terms only used qualitatively in Part 1 (the 'door is trust, held by <holder>' seams never name 'calibration'), so they are payoff not re-announcement -- the maintainer block confirms this deferral is deliberate ('the reveal is the smart reader's to make first'). Bullet 3 (53, 'High reach splits on calibration...') adds the split's two named outcome states, not previously stated. Bullet 4 (54, 'The frontier moves outward...Push reach past calibration and you are checking less, not delegating more') adds the frontier concept plus a distinct prescriptive warning not covered by bullet 3. Each bullet clears the 'what does this add' test: a definition, a definition, a split-outcome, a caution. (b) self-referential design commentary: none of the four bullets discuss the curriculum's own pedagogy or design choices -- all four are substantive claims about the delegation model itself. (c) aphorism kicker: bullet 4's second clause has a pithy contrastive shape but introduces new content (the checking-vs-delegating reframe) rather than restating the chunk header or a stated point line, so it is not a koan that carries nothing.
